rubric.question: 逐句：自然 / 有点怪 / 很怪。书面腔、讲解腔、翻译腔、念稿感、报菜名式罗列都算怪

rubric.name: Flow and transitions
rubric.question: Cold open, the 'what's coming' part, chapter changes, before/after examples: does it sound like one person following a thought, not 'Point one…' templates or a TOC read aloud? Do adjacent lines connect?

rubric.name: Clear on one hearing
rubric.question: Ear only: one new idea per line; clear reference ('this' points to something); terms explained before used; numbers and words not misheard

rubric.name: Tight
rubric.question: No filler, repetition, or empty truisms; point out lines that could go without losing anything

rubric.name: Voice and rhythm
rubric.question: One warm, clear, unpretentious narrator throughout; varied sentence length; each line sayable in one breath

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every 'a bit off' / 'clearly off' line, a drop-in rewrite no longer than the original; rank the 5 most awkward lines

items.law_name: 中文屏幕文字（PPT 式画面）
items.checks: 逐屏看画面上的中文字：是不是只列纲要、够不够简练、和口播有没有分工、看不看得完。
items.how: 硬上限（超了必须报）：标题 ≤12 字；其余每块 ≤16 字；同屏文字块 ≤4 块（不含页眉小标签、出处与图表刻度）；一屏总字数 ≤36 字。屏幕下方还有口播字幕，观众要同时看。
items.what: 逐屏看画面上的中文字：是不是只列纲要、够不够简练、和口播有没有分工、看不看得完。
items.problem: 上一版屏幕文字很多是整句（如「另训一个模型，在两家医院的片子上认医院的准确率——胸片里藏着医院的“指纹”」），等于把口播又印了一遍；用户要求画面只列纲要、相对简练（2026-11-08）。

rubric.name: 只列纲要
rubric.question: 每屏只放关键词、短语、关键数字、标签；不是口播整句的复述。按硬上限逐屏数字数，超了就报

items.how: Hard limits (report every breach): title ≤6 words; any other block ≤9 words; ≤4 text blocks per screen (not counting the small eyebrow label, source line or chart ticks); ≤22 words per screen. Narration subtitles also sit at the bottom of the frame.
items.what: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.problem: The previous version put full sentences on screen (e.g. 'A separate model identified the hospital for scans from two hospitals — a hospital fingerprint'), repeating the narration. The user wants outline-only, concise slides (2026-11-08).

rubric.name: Outline, not prose
rubric.question: Only keywords, short phrases, key numbers, labels; no full narration sentences. Count words per screen against the hard limits

rubric.name: Divided from narration
rubric.question: Screen carries structure, numbers, contrasts; narration explains. No verbatim repetition, no new claims the narration doesn't make; terms match the narration

rubric.name: Hierarchy and consistency
rubric.question: What reads first, second; ≤3 levels (title, point, note); numbering, labels, chapter names and agenda items consistent with each other

rubric.name: Native phrasing and style
rubric.question: Sentence case headline style; no Chinglish; consistent punctuation (no trailing periods on fragments), en dashes, quotes; parallel grammar in lists

rubric.name: Readable in time
rubric.question: From the screenshot and how long it stays: readable in time (~3 words/s while also reading subtitles and the chart)

Blocks over 9 words: l13 (13), l27 caption (20), l31 caption (14), l35 body (17), l47 h2 (14), l48 body (21), l49 h2 (10), l50 body (18), l52 caption (17), l53 captions (17, 19), l54 (13), l55 (13, 13). Screen totals over 22 words: l10 33, l22 34, l23 37, l27 38, l35 31, l38 35, l39 58, l47 29, l48 50, l50 41, l52 27, l53 46, l54 45, l55 62. The agenda card has a title, 4 rows, a 3-item prereq card and a note (roughly 9 blocks, ~50 words). Chapters 5–6 are the worst: the s9 captions are narration-length sentences ("Choose models and catch overfitting on the validation set; save the test set for one final check").

P2.evidence: The screen repeats the narration on l09 (21-word h1 vs "learns the flukes, too, and does worse on new data"), l13 ("Find the pattern in these points, to predict data it has never seen"), l27 (caption "Where the analogy breaks: the student knows he's memorizing. The model doesn't — it's simply powerful enough to remember every point." vs l27 narration), l41 (full narration line), l47 ("A separate model identified the hospital for scans from two hospitals — a hospital fingerprint", the exact sentence the user already rejected), l48 body, l50 h1, l52–l53 captions, and the agenda rows (= l04–l07 verbatim). Term drift: screen "accidents" vs narration "flukes" (l09), then "noise" (l12). l54 introduces "40" (points), which the narration never says; l31 adds "we take the median", which the narration does not say. Good counter-examples exist (l01–l02, l24, l26, l36, l45, l49 numbers carry the screen while the narration explains).

P3.evidence: Chapter numbering contradicts itself. card_c_fix shows "06 · How to spot and prevent it" and the dot strip lists 6 chapters (Problem, Analogy, Experiment, Lens, Real world, Fixes), but s9 eyebrow reads "05 · HOW TO PREVENT IT" and s8 (Real world) has no number at all. The agenda lists only 4 of the 6 chapters (no Experiment; "Real failures, and how to avoid them" merges two chapters). Card titles do not match the eyebrows ("What problem is this?" vs "01 · THE PROBLEM"; "Let's run an experiment" vs "03 · THE EXPERIMENT"; "How to spot and prevent it" vs "HOW TO PREVENT IT"). More than 3 levels on l47/l48 (display 99.9%+, h2, body, red line, source) and l50 (eyebrow, h1, body, tabs). l23 has two h2 lines and no title.

P4.evidence: Headlines are mostly sentence case and the register is natural ("Falls apart", "Keep a mock exam", "Part flu detector, part winter detector"). Flaws: spaced em dashes instead of en dashes (l23 "bad on both — easy to spot", l47, l53, l27, agenda note); trailing periods on fragments/captions (l09, l27, l53, agenda note "…in a sentence.") while other captions have none; mixed apostrophes (straight "model's" on l48, curly "shouldn’t" on l53); "vs" (l48) vs "vs." (agenda); "Valid." abbreviation next to full "validation set"; non-parallel lists (agenda: clause / clause / noun phrase / noun phrase; three ways: imperative / noun phrase / imperative; chapter cards: question / noun / imperative-ish). l29 "Photos he has seen: all right" is unclear. l43 "1152" vs narration "about 1,100" (no thousands separator).

P5.evidence: Several screens ask for far more than ~3 words/s plus subtitles. l50: 41 words in 11.9 s (3.4 w/s, 3 stacked blocks). l55: 62 words in 8.6 s, with three captions the viewer must re-read to find the new one. l39: 58 tokens in 9.1 s (about 30 of them numerals). l48: 50 words with the h2 still showing while the new 34% vs 1% line arrives. l35: 31 words in 10.2 s. Layout defects from the PNGs: l31 title is clipped at the right edge ("what happens t…", 10 words at 76 px on one line); l55 third card is cut off at the right edge; l37/l39 title touches the right edge; l19 "Exam points" label sits on top of chart markers; l31 axis label is clipped at the bottom; l27, l53 and the l48/l43 source line sit at y≈840–880 where the burned-in subtitles go. Fine screens: l01, l02, l11, l24, l36, l41, l51 (a few words, long hold).

P6.evidence: Drop-in rewrites are given for every breach and awkward phrase in the issues table below (each is shorter than the original and keeps the narration's terms).

P5.evidence: l18’s question is clipped; l31–l35’s heading is clipped; l53 introduces a 19-word confession during 6.2 seconds, already requiring about 6.3 seconds at 3 words/s before subtitles.

P4.judge_reason: Both reviewers gave 2, but the shared blind spots go past minor flaws. l31–l35 title "As models get more complex, what happens to the errors" is a question with no question mark (s6.html data-en has none). l37–l39 "How many numbers to remember ten points?" is ungrammatical, and it spells out "ten" next to "10 heights" / "10 numbers". l54–l55 "More, and more varied, data" is a stilted spoken parenthetical, and it is not parallel with "Keep a mock exam" / "Put limits on complexity". l43 "50M search terms → 1152 data points" uses an arrow that reads as a conversion, not a mismatch. The l37–l39 tables use hyphen-minus ("-0.49") beside true plus signs. Add a's confirmed items: em dashes against the en-dash house style (l23, l27, l47, l53, agenda), mixed straight/curly apostrophes (l48 vs l53), "vs" (l48) vs "vs." (agenda), and the l29 "all right" calque of 全对. A native editor would wince at several of these, so this is a 1.

P6.judge_reason: Both reports give broad rewrites, but neither earns 3. a claims "every breach" yet has no row for l22 (34 words), l38 (35), l26 (12 blocks) or the apostrophe and "vs" inconsistencies. Some of a's rewrites are worse than the original: l50 "Right clue, wrong setting" misstates shortcut learning, and l52 "Choose models on Valid." reuses the abbreviation a itself flagged. b covers almost every screen, but l02 collapses the "Nearly perfect / Falls apart" contrast that b says to keep. b's l27 "Model: capacity without awareness" is abstract jargon. b's l48 drops "34% vs 1%", the number the screen should carry. Neither report gives a rewrite for the missed P4 items above.
